population.definition: Population of the Special Zone of Conakry (comprising five core urban communes: Kaloum, Dixinn, Matam, Ratoma, and Matoto) recorded in the 3rd General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-3, March 2014) conducted by the Institut National de la Statistique (INS) of Guinea, tabulated via CityPopulation. Extended agglomeration mapping numbered 1,940,544, with contemporary estimates surpassing 2.5 million.

source.title: Guinea: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2014)
source.quote: 2014-03-01 | Conakry Special Zone: 1,660,973; Greater urban area: 1,940,544

facts.claim: Conakry was founded in 1887 on Tombo Island, later connected by a causeway to the Kaloum Peninsula, succeeding Benty in 1904 as the colonial capital of French Guinea.

source.title: Guinea: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2014)
source.quote: Founded on Tombo Island and became capital in 1904

facts.claim: The Grande Mosquée de Conakry, inaugurated in 1982 by President Ahmed Sékou Touré with support from King Fahd of Saudi Arabia, is one of the largest mosques in sub-Saharan Africa, accommodating over 25,000 worshippers.

source.title: Patrimoine culturel de Conakry: Musée de Sandervalia et Grande Mosquée
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l'Artisanat de Guinée
source.quote: Grande Mosquée de Conakry inaugurée en 1982 pouvant accueillir 25 000 fidèles

facts.claim: The Musée National de Sandervalia in Kaloum houses irreplaceable artistic treasures of the coastal Guinea peoples, including monumental shoulder masks (D'mba / Nimba) of the Baga tradition and ancient musical instruments.

source.title: Patrimoine culturel de Conakry: Musée de Sandervalia et Grande Mosquée
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l'Artisanat de Guinée
source.quote: Musée de Sandervalia abritant les célèbres masques Nimba des Baga
